headline: MyFace Group for 'People Who Peaked in Middle School (But in a Chill Way)' Goes Viral
subheadline: Supportive community celebrates members' 'glory days' of ages 11-14
summary: A MyFace support group for people whose best years were decidedly early has found an unexpectedly wholesome niche.
content:
A MyFace group titled "We Peaked in Middle School (But We're Chill About It)" has gone viral after users discovered its surprisingly supportive community of people who freely admit their best days are behind them—way behind them.

The group, which has grown to 87,000 members, provides a space for people to share memories from ages 11-14 when they were, in their words, "absolutely crushing it."

"I won the school spelling bee in 7th grade," shared one member. "I've never felt that alive since. And that's okay. Some of us bloom early."

The group maintains strict rules against negativity. Members are encouraged to celebrate their middle school achievements without shame, whether those achievements were academic, athletic, social, or "being really good at Snake on a Nokia."

"I was the fastest typer in computer class," wrote another member. "47 words per minute. I've since learned that doesn't matter in life. But for one semester, I was a god."

What sets the community apart is its genuine acceptance. Unlike similar groups that traffic in irony, members appear to sincerely support each other's early-life accomplishments.

"Society tells us we should peak in our 20s or 30s," explained group founder @8thGradeGoddess. "But some of us peaked at 13, and that's valid. We had our moment. Now we're just vibing."

The group hosts weekly "Throwback Thursdays" where members share yearbook photos and stories of middle school triumphs. A recent thread about "the time I got 847 points on the pacer test" received 3,000 supportive comments.

Psychologists have praised the community's approach. "There's freedom in accepting your peak," noted one. "These people aren't sad. They're at peace. That's healthier than most of us."

At press time, the group was planning its first reunion. Location: a middle school gymnasium.
author: Chris Patterson, Human Interest
